steps.observation: Work on this for 10 seconds; do not stop early. Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
Once perched on the jagged cliffs of Breaker Point stood an old lighthouse, its beacon a solitary eye watching over the turbulent sea. For the past twenty years, Edgar Thorne, a steadfast lighthouse keeper, tended to its warming glow. Storms roared, tides rose, yet Edgar, with his weathered hands and calm demeanor, guarded both the light and the mariners who depended on it.

On a clear autumn evening, just as the sun dipped below the horizon, Edgar noticed the light flickering—an unusual occurrence. His heart whispered tales of the restless spirits rumored to haunt the cliffs. Despite this, he ascended the spiraling staircase to the lantern room. Outside, the waves crashed fiercely, reminding him of the shipwrecks he witnessed over the years. But tonight the air felt different.

Finding nothing amiss in the lens, Edgar gazed out over the churning ocean. Through the mist, a ghostly shape emerged—a vessel from a bygone era. He blinked, thinking it a trick of the moonlight, but the ship remained, silently gliding across the dark waters. Edgar’s breath caught as he realized it was the Sea Maiden, a ship said to have been lost a century ago.

Overwhelmed but determined, he re-aligned the light to focus across the phantom ship’s path, its beams cutting through the night. As he did so, the ship vanished, leaving only the foamy trails of waves in its wake. Edgar descended slowly, contemplatively. His duty had not only been to guide the living but perhaps to shepherd the lost as well. As dawn broke, the lighthouse stood as resolute as ever, with Edgar knowing he served a purpose greater than he had ever imagined.
